article_content: 'Bob Greene explores why we watch sports, highlighting LeBron James as an example of the difference between standard effort and true excellence. He notes that while the outcome of the NBA All-Star Game is forgettable, its real appeal lies in celebrating the best in basketball. Greene reminds us that despite scandals involving players like Alex Rodriguez and Barry Bonds, we remain captivated because of the tissue-thin difference between a job merely done and a job done well. John Updike, who died at 76, famously captured this in his remark about Ted Williams, praising the power of small efforts that elevate performance. That same principle applies to everyday life as we decide whether to add a bit more energy, pride, and diligence to each task. We watch to witness those rare flashes of brilliance—a player’s unexpected lunge or additional thrust on the court—because it resonates with our own potential for excellence. The applause star athletes receive may not mirror our daily reality, but the aspiration to go beyond mere adequacy is universal. Greene concludes that we watch for these fleeting yet inspiring moments that remind us of what we, too, can strive for in our own lives.'

article_content: American-born beautician, 31-year-old Janee Parsons, was found fatally stabbed inside her family home in Bicester, Oxfordshire, leaving relatives reeling with grief as her husband, Andrew Parsons, stands charged with her murder. Her sister, Jocelyn Brady, said part of her own life ended when Janee died, and her biological father, John Jacks, described feeling a tremendous gap in his heart. Mrs Parsons, a mother of two young boys, was discovered by police after neighbors heard alarming screams and called 999. Andrew Parsons, 38, was with his severely injured wife at their rental house when authorities arrived. He has been remanded in custody and faces a hearing at Oxford Crown Court on February 11, when he is expected to enter a plea. Janee’s mother, Mary Brady, remembered her daughter as a ‘great gift from God’ and a ‘tireless worker’ who would be deeply missed. Her adopted father, Phil Brady, said she left a profound mark on everyone she met, and her sister described her as ‘passionate, vivacious, and magnetic.’ According to relatives, Janee was determined from a young age, always striving to be the best in everything she did. The shocking incident has shaken the local community, and neighbors expressed concern for her two children. Reports suggest the family may have faced financial setbacks. They lived in the UK after Janee sold her Oklahoma spa business, and the couple recently started separate ventures: Andrew launched a heat pumps firm, while Janee set up Wink Ink Ltd. Her expertise in makeup and skincare extended to professional modeling shoots and wedding events in both the US and Britain. Police confirmed that they could not accept comments regarding the case for legal reasons.

article_content: 'Satya Nadella, CEO of Microsoft, showcased his passion for cricket during the Microsoft Ignite 2023 keynote. He mentioned staying up all night to watch the Cricket World Cup semi-final match between India and New Zealand, which finished just five minutes before Ignite kicked off. He jokingly noted that the conference was scheduled on the same day as the World Cup semi-final.' 'Nadella highlighted that this World Cup match was a shorter version of the game compared to Test cricket, which can last up to five days. He has often credited cricket with helping him understand teamwork and leadership.' 'A tweet from Pavan Jha thanked Mohammed Shami for wrapping up the match in time, allowing Nadella to start his keynote on schedule. India defeated New Zealand, securing a place in the final stage of the tournament.' 'Notably, Nadella has a history of involvement in cricket. He played for his school team and has recently partnered with the Delhi Capitals IPL team. He also co-owns the Seattle Orcas franchise in Major League Cricket (MLC), which aims to support the growth of cricket in the United States.' 'Nadella plans to build a cricket stadium in Seattle, and Microsoft’s Redmond campus now boasts an oval-shaped cricket ground. Other tech leaders who share a passion for cricket include Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet and Google, who once dreamed of becoming a cricketer.'

article_content: Barack Obama frequently talks about helping the job market recover, but he took a direct approach when he spoke with a woman who asked about her husband’s unemployment. During a Google+ Hangout, he encouraged her to send him her husband’s CV, saying he wanted to see why the man struggled to find work as a semiconductor engineer. Jennifer Wedel, 29, from Fort Worth, Texas, said her 40-year-old husband had been unemployed for three years despite expertise in a high-demand field. She questioned why foreign workers were still receiving visas for high-skilled jobs while her husband remained jobless. She described herself as a Republican who did not vote for Obama previously but felt unimpressed with the current GOP candidates, suggesting she might support Obama this time. Mrs. Wedel works for State Farm, and her husband was with Texas Instruments for seven years before losing his job. Obama participated in a live video chat called a Google+ Hangout, answering questions from YouTube users and speaking directly with five participants, including Mrs. Wedel. This formed part of the White House’s social media outreach following the State of the Union. Their conversation touched on job creation, the economy, and the President’s stance on innovation. An Occupy protester told Obama he was 53 and needed help finding work, to which Obama emphasized the importance of growing the economy. Obama defended the use of unmanned drone strikes, claiming they are carefully targeted at known terrorists. He also addressed questions about online piracy and said it is possible to protect intellectual property without compromising internet openness. The conversation occurred a day before the Republican primary in Florida, where GOP candidates Mitt Romney and Newt Gingrich continued to criticize Obama. None of the questions directly addressed the presidential race but focused on issues like jobs and daily concerns. Mrs. Wedel also asked if the President would showcase his dance skills, which he declined, joking that First Lady Michelle Obama teases him about his dancing. He mentioned their upcoming 20th wedding anniversary, noting it might not be very romantic due to the election season. Over 133,000 questions were submitted and ranked on YouTube, but although many focused on the legalization of marijuana, that topic was not selected for the Hangout discussion. One of the top-voted questions concerned the potential extradition of Richard O’Dwyer, a British student accused of copyright infringement. Obama noted he was not personally involved in the O’Dwyer case but emphasized protecting intellectual property in a manner that remains consistent with internet freedom. O’Dwyer’s mother criticized what she viewed as the aggressive use of extradition laws by the U.S., drawing parallels to the Gary McKinnon hacking case.

ئەو مەهەندەسەی سەمیکۆنداکتەرەچیە. جێنیفەر وێدێل، ٢٩ ساڵە، خەلکی فۆرت وۆرتی تێکساز، وتی مێردەکەی ٤٠ ساڵە تەواو ٣ ساڵە بێ کارە، هەرچەند دەزانرێت هونوەرە بەرزی هەیە لە بواری باڵا. ئەو پرسی بۆچی هێشتا وەک ژێدەرگشتی Occupy وتی ٥٣ ساڵەمە و بەکار ناکەم. ئۆباما جێگیر کرد گرنگترین کار ئەوەیە ئابووری ببەرزین. ئۆباما بە بەکاربردنی ترۆن (drone) ووت کە هێرشەکانیان بە مەبەستی سەرەتایی بوون بۆ تێکشکاندنی تەندروستی تێکۆشان. هەروەها گفتووگۆ لەسەر کارێکی ئینتەرنێتی قچسکراو بوو کە یاسای ھەڵگەڕان بۆ هیچ ناوخۆی ئینتەرنێت سەر نوێتەوە نەگرێ. گفتوگۆکە لە ڕۆژی پێش دەنگگرتنی رێپەبلێکانیەکانی فلۆریدا لەگەڵ هێرشی زۆر لە لایەن میت ڕۆمنی و نیوت گینگریچ بەرامبەر ئۆباما. هەرچی بوو، پرسیارەکان سەر باری کار و ژیان بوون نە سەر هەڵبژاردنی سەرۆکایت. خانمی وێدێل پرس لە ئۆباما کە رقصی خۆی بنیشاند وەکو تایبەتمەندی، بەڵام بوو، قوتابی بەریتانییەکی تۆمەتبار بە کۆپیڕایت. ئۆباما ووت کو کاری بۆ ئەو کەیسە ناکات بە شێوەی رێگەگرتنی مافی زانیاری و چاودێری ئینتەرنێت. دایکی ئۆدوایەر ووت ئەم یاسایە زۆر بە ئاگەر دووبارە بەکار دێت، وەکو هەردوو چۆنەتی گری مەکینن. ئەو بە چاوەڕوانی ئازادی گەب دەکرد.

article_content: Paragraph 1: 'A renewed debate has emerged around yearly mammograms for breast cancer screening after fresh findings from a Canadian study drew criticism. The Canadian National Breast Screening Study, which tracked participants for 25 years, determined that annual mammograms for women between 40 and 59 do not lower breast cancer death rates beyond what physical exams or typical care achieve, provided post-surgical treatments are readily available. Researchers published these outcomes in the British Medical Journal.' Paragraph 2: 'Several professional societies and experts question these conclusions, highlighting that this long-running study has released data periodically for over two decades. The project began collecting screening information in six Canadian provinces from 1980 to 1985, enrolling close to 90,000 women aged 40 to 59. Participants were split into two groups: an experimental one receiving yearly mammograms and a control group without them.' Paragraph 3: 'After exhaustive follow-up over 25 years, the results for both groups appear remarkably similar. Within the mammography group, 666 invasive breast cancers were diagnosed, while 524 appeared in the control group. Meanwhile, 180 patient deaths from breast cancer were recorded in the mammography group compared to 171 in the control group.' Paragraph 4: 'The survival rates diverge between the two groups: 70.6% of women diagnosed in the mammography group lived at least 25 years, while 62.8% in the control group survived as long. Study authors attribute this difference to a combination of lead time, length time bias, and overdiagnosis. In fact, they concluded that 22% of invasive cancers identified through screening likely would not have endangered the patients during their lifetimes.' Paragraph 5: 'According to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, about 38.7 million mammogram procedures take place annually in the United States. Data also indicate that 75% of women over 40 reported having a mammogram within the last two years. Yet, a joint statement from the American College of Radiology and the Society of Breast Imaging calls the newly published CNBSS report highly misleading, arguing it is based on flawed and outdated procedures.' Paragraph 6: 'Critics of the CNBSS point out that the equipment used was older technology, and that untrained technicians handled the initial screenings. Dr. Otis Brawley, chief medical officer for the American Cancer Society, notes the randomization process was not done properly. Consequently, major professional organizations advise against using these findings to influence screening policies, fearing that many women could face greater risks if guidelines changed.' Paragraph 7: 'Overdiagnosis—identifying cancers that would never become problematic—remains a known hazard in cancer screenings. Dr. H. Gilbert Welch, who co-wrote Overdiagnosed: Making People Sick in the Pursuit of Health, employs a metaphor of turtles (slow, harmless cancers), rabbits (potentially treatable), and birds (aggressive cancers that have spread before detection). He cautions that tests sometimes catch harmless “turtles,” leading to unnecessary treatments like chemotherapy or surgery.' Paragraph 8: 'The National Health Service in the UK finds that for each woman saved by routine mammography, three receive a diagnosis of a non-threatening cancer. Currently, the American Cancer Society recommends annual mammogram exams beginning at age 40, in addition to clinical breast checks every three years for those over age 20. The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force advises women aged 50 to 75 to have biennial screenings and suggests younger women seek individualized guidance. Both agencies are reviewing recent research and may update their guidelines. Dr. Brawley, an oncologist, believes there is some benefit to mammography, but emphasizes that women should understand the limits of these tests so they can make informed choices. He also notes that most cancers are ultimately preventable.'

كەناڤادا هێلکەوتنی سوتاند. یاسایی نێودەوڵەتی سكرینی تومووری مەمه‌ (CNBSS)، كە 25 ساڵ بەشداربووانی تاقیكردنه‌وه‌ گێڕاو بوون، ووتی ماماگڕامی هاوساڵانە بۆ ژنانی 40 تا 59 ساڵ زیاتر نایە كۆچی دوایی تومووری مەمه‌ لەوەی بڕوانامی كەسێك له پزیشکی حاجایە یاخود چاودێری گشتی ببێت، به شرطی ئەوەی چاره‌سەری دواتر لە بەدۆزرانده‌وه‌ی توموور هەیە. ئەم ئەنجامانە لە ڕۆژنامەی تیبی بریتیش بڵاوكرانەوە. چەند رێكخراو و چالاكوانی زانستی هاتن ئاڕاستەی ئەم ووتارە، بەڵام پێشبینی دەكرێ تاقیكردنه‌وه‌كه‌ زیادلە دوو ده‌هەكەوت ئەنجام دراو بێت. لە ساڵانی 1980 تا 1985، ئەم پڕۆگرامی سكرینینگە لە شاشەی شەش ئۆستانی كەناڤادا داتا گرت، كە ناوە 90,000 ژنانی 40 تا 59 ساڵ تێكدێ كران. هاوڵاتییان بە دوو گروپ دابەشكرا: گروپی تاقیكردنه‌وه‌ ماڵی هاوساڵانی ماماگڕام و گروپی كنترۆل كە ه هیچ ماماگڕامێكیان وەرناگرت. دوای 25 ساڵ ئەم دوو گروپە ئەنجامەكانی كومالە جیاوازیان نەگێڕا. لە گروپی ماماگڕامدا، 666 تومووری مەمه‌ی هێرشی هاتبوونە رۆشنایی، لەم کاتدا 524 توموور لە گروپی كنترۆل وەردەست بون. هەروەها، 180 كەلە گروپی ماماگڕام مردبوون بە هۆی تومووری مەمه‌دا، کە ئەو ژمارەیە لە گروپی كنترۆلدا 171 بوون. رێژەی ماوەی ژیان بۆ ئەم دوو گروپەی تومووری مەمه‌ جیاواز بوو: 70.6% لە ژنانی گروپی ماماگڕام 25 ساڵ زیندوو مایەوە، کەتێدایە 62.8% لەكەسی گروپی كنترۆل هەمان کات ژیان دەكات. ئەو نووسه‌رانەی تاقیكردنه‌وه‌كه‌ ئەم جیاوازییەیان باسكردووە بە كاتی پێشوو و درێژخایەنی كات و زیادیشكردن لە دۆزینەوە. ئەوان هەروەها راگەیاندن 22% لە توموورە هێرشیه‌كان لە ڕێی سكرینینگه‌وه‌ وەردەست بوون بێ گێرانەوە بۆ ژیان. بەپێی هەڵسەنگاندنی دۆسەڵاتی خواردنی و دەرمانسازی ئه‌مریکا (FDA)، لە مەڵكەی ئه‌مریکا هەر ساڵ نزیکەی 38.7 ملیۆن كۆی ماماگڕام دەكرێت. هەروەها ڕاپۆرتەكان دەبینن 75% ژنانی ژێر 40 ساڵ لە دوو ساڵی ڕابردودا ماماگڕامیان وەرگرتووە. لە یەك بەیاننامەی هاوكێشكردووەدا، كۆلەیجی ڕادیۆلۆژیی ئه‌مریكا و كۆمەڵگای سكرینینی مەمه‌ ئەم تاقیكردنه‌وه‌ی نوێیان 'گومڕەكاندنەوەیەكی زۆر' ناونێن، بە هۆی تەكنەلۆجیا و ڕێنیشاندنی پێگەهێنان ئەگەر كێشە وەردەگرێت. ئەو دانیشتنە نوێیان بەشداری كردووە وتووە لىهەروەها ھەڵسەنگاندنی یاساییان هەبێت، دكتۆر ئوتیس براولی، وه‌زیری تیبی كۆماری كێنسری ئه‌مریكا دیاری دەكات رێكخراوە زۆریان لەبەر ماوە، هەروەها ڕێكخراوە ناو میدیای زانیارییەكانیش نوقە بۆ گۆڕینی یاساوەكان دەزانن. یان بە ترسدا دەڵێن ئەوها هەندێك زن فریدەكانیان زیات دەگات. بەبۆنەیەكی دێرین لە تاقیكردنه‌وه‌ی هەموو جۆرە کێنسەرەكانیش، گۆچەكان دەكرێت سكان پێبدەن كە هێشت نەبوو ڕێگەداندا. دكتۆر ه. گیلبېرت وێلچ ھاو نووسینی 'Overdiagnosed: Making People Sick in the Pursuit of Health' هەروەها بۆ مەترسی فێربوونی تومووری ئەویزمان دەكات، بۆ ناو فڕۆکە دروستەكان. ڕێكخراوی خزمەتگوزاری تەندروستی نێو دۆڵەی بەریتانیا (NHS) وتووە بۆ هەر ژنێك چیتر هەر سێ كەس توموور لە مێردنی نجات دەدات لە ڕێی ماماگڕامدا، تریش تێدا هەیە كە لە دەسته‌شاندنی جێتۆرەكان. كۆماری كەنسری ئه‌مریكا داوا دەكات ژنان لە 40 ساڵەوە ماماگڕامی هاوساڵانە بکەن، بەرەوچوون پشكنینی مەمه‌ همێشە بە دوو و سێ ساڵدا ئەنجام دەدرێت بۆ ئەوانی چەند ساڵ گەورەتر. هەروەها كۆمەڵی پاراستنی تەندروستی ئەمریكا وتووی كۆتایی بە دوو ساڵ جارێك كرێ بۆ تاقیكردنه‌وه‌كانی تومووری مەمه‌ بۆ ژنانی 50 تا 75 ساڵ، دووبارە جوانكردنەوە بۆ ئەوانەی زیر 50 ساڵكەوت بەشێوەیەكی نهێنی تەفسیركراو. دوا، هەردوو رێكخراوەكان ئاڕاستەیان گرتووە بۆ چاوپێكردنەوەی هێلانەكان. دكتۆر براولی وشەی مەزن ئەنجام دەدات كە زۆر فواید هەیە بۆ ماماگڕام، بەڵام دەڵێ ژنانیش لێربكرن هزری كەسایەتییان بكەن بۆ بربەشوندنی کێنسەرەكان.

          'Marseille coach Didier Deschamps turned to Remy as a replacement for Mamadou Niang, who joined Turkish side Fenerbahce this week, after being discouraged by the price of Sevilla s Brazilian World Cup star Luis Fabiano.',
          'Ivory Coast striker Bakari Kone and former Spain forward Fernando Morientes have also left Marseille since last season.',
          'Deschamps noted he hoped to bring in an international-caliber striker like Fabiano, but the cost was too high, stating that if the price is unreasonable, the club must stop negotiations.',
          'Remy, who signed a five-year contract and was courted by English clubs such as Stoke and West Ham, cited Marseille s involvement in the UEFA Champions League as a key factor.',
          'Marseille had also been linked with another France international striker, Andre-Pierre Gignac, but his club released a statement denying any formal offer.',
          'Meanwhile, Arsenal were told to improve their offer for France defender Sebastien Squillaci, who was left out of Sevilla s Champions League qualifier to avoid being cup-tied.',
          'Nikica Jelavic of Rapid Vienna is set to join Rangers, and Slovakia s World Cup star Vladimir Weiss will move there on loan from Manchester City.',
          'Liverpool excluded Argentina international Javier Mascherano from their Europa League match, with manager Roy Hodgson insisting he will not let him leave unless a suitable offer emerges. Manchester City beat Timisoara 1-0 thanks to a debut goal from Mario Balotelli.',
          'In other Europa League results, Sibir Novosibirsk defeated PSV 1-0, Bayer Leverkusen won 3-0 against Tavriya Simferopol with a late penalty from Michael Ballack, Juventus secured a 2-1 victory at Sturm Graz, and Turkish sides Fenerbahce and Galatasaray failed to notch wins.',
          'Stuttgart and Borussia Dortmund both emerged victorious, with Dortmund beating FK Karabakh 4-0 as Paraguay striker Lucas Barrios and Japanese forward Shinji Kagawa scored. Celtic overcame Utrecht 2-0, Porto won 3-0 at Racing Genk, and Denmark s Brondby stunned Sporting Lisbon 2-0 in Portugal.'
